title: SAP Agent Context repository vision
wedge: A cloneable, local-first, agent-first SAP context runtime with evidence-backed JSONL records and fail-closed boundaries; not a SAP documentation mirror, human wiki, generic vector demo, tenant configuration store, or fluent SAP chatbot.
north_star: SAP professionals can clone sap-agent-context, run local gates, and give agents enough structured SAP context to reason from zero without inventing tenant, release, customizing, role, availability, or production facts.
desired_outcome: Make the repository the practical local context substrate for SAP agents: compact records, source-labelled claims, rebuildable indexes, deterministic gates, query/answer contracts, and actionable gap reports that steer future curation work.
target_user_audience: AI agents working on SAP functional design, field mapping, workflow, roles, migration, integration, analytics, EAM/PM, and implementation support
SAP professionals using agents who need grounded local context without copying SAP proprietary documentation
Repo maintainers deciding which domains are mature enough for retrieval, bundle generation, or deterministic answer contracts
painful_moment: Generic model memory can produce plausible SAP-sounding output, but SAP implementation work needs source/access/freshness boundaries, tenant/release caveats, and local evidence that fails closed when proof is missing.
core_promise: Clone the repo, build the local index, query or bundle context, and get compact source-labelled SAP evidence plus explicit gaps instead of copied docs, hidden assumptions, or hallucinated tenant truth.
principles: Agent-first: optimize records, bundles, indexes, schemas, fixtures, and machine-readable examples before human prose.
JSON/JSONL-first: records/*.jsonl and JSON reports/examples are canonical for agents; Markdown is narrative maintainer context only.
Evidence before coverage: a small source-labelled domain slice with fixtures beats broad unverified item count growth.
Fail closed on tenant, release, customizing, authorization, role, availability, production behavior, and gated SAP Note/KBA claims.
Retrieval is product: important prompts need positive and negative fixtures or query smokes, not just stored records.
Public-safe by construction: no customer data, tenant URLs, screenshots, SAP exports, credentials, or proprietary copied SAP documentation.
Gaps must steer work: reports should classify missing source, freshness, retrieval, fixture, rule, or maturity evidence into actionable next slices.
non_goals: Do not mirror SAP Help, Learning Hub, SAP Notes/KBA, SAP for Me, or copied proprietary documentation.
Do not become a human browsing wiki or training manual as the primary product surface.
Do not store tenant configuration, customer mappings, internal URLs, screenshots, credentials, or SAP exports.
Do not optimize for item count, domain breadth, or fluent prose over source-labelled evidence and gates.
Do not claim globally exhaustive SAP correctness or current release truth from repo-level audits.
Do not add broad LLM answer generation before deterministic retrieval/evidence/answer contracts are mature.
Do not hand-edit generated build artifacts as source of truth.

load_bearing_assumptions.claim: A compact public-safe context graph can make SAP agent work materially better without copying SAP documentation.
load_bearing_assumptions.fails_if: Useful SAP work repeatedly requires copied proprietary text, gated SAP Notes/KBA content, tenant screenshots, or customer-specific mappings.
load_bearing_assumptions.cheapest_test: Run representative query/bundle/answer fixtures and manually inspect whether source pointers, claims, and caveats give enough context for useful first-pass agent output.
load_bearing_assumptions.kill_or_pivot: If public-safe pointers are insufficient for a domain, mark that domain gated/needs_curation and require authorized human verification rather than expanding public-ready records.

load_bearing_assumptions.claim: Local rebuildable indexes plus FTS/vector retrieval can serve as the practical runtime without hosted retrieval services.
load_bearing_assumptions.fails_if: Fresh clone workflows become too slow, flaky, or dependent on external hosted services for default usage.
load_bearing_assumptions.cheapest_test: Run uv sync --locked, make check, build-index, build-embeddings, and representative runtime-search/query-explain commands on a clean local clone.
load_bearing_assumptions.kill_or_pivot: If local runtime cost becomes unacceptable, split heavy optional artifacts behind explicit commands while keeping default validation and basic retrieval local.

load_bearing_assumptions.claim: Structured curation gates can improve trust faster than broad content additions.
load_bearing_assumptions.fails_if: Gap, maturity, or curation reports do not produce actionable next slices, or teams still add shallow records to make numbers look better.
load_bearing_assumptions.cheapest_test: Run curation-report and audit-completeness after each slice; classify failures as missing source, freshness, retrieval, fixture, schema, or maturity work.
load_bearing_assumptions.kill_or_pivot: If reports are noisy or non-actionable, pause domain expansion and improve report schemas/thresholds before adding more records.

load_bearing_assumptions.claim: Deterministic consumer contracts should precede broad LLM generation.
load_bearing_assumptions.fails_if: Downstream consumers cannot use bundles, query examples, or consultant-answer artifacts without hidden assumptions or manual interpretation.
load_bearing_assumptions.cheapest_test: Add JSON consumer examples and run a downstream-agent dry run using only status, citations, evidence, boundary, and gap fields.
load_bearing_assumptions.kill_or_pivot: If consumer output still needs free-form interpretation, strengthen schemas and examples before adding an LLM layer.

load_bearing_assumptions.claim: SAP Agent Context can stay repo-sized and maintainable while covering multiple high-value SAP lenses.
load_bearing_assumptions.fails_if: Schema, fixtures, support profiles, or ranking rules become brittle, duplicated, or too slow as domains expand.
load_bearing_assumptions.cheapest_test: Before each domain slice, measure changed files, fixture count, test runtime, and whether logic moved from code to reusable data contracts when patterns repeat.
load_bearing_assumptions.kill_or_pivot: If hardcoded profiles or fixtures become brittle, introduce data-driven schemas before adding another domain.

success_metrics: Fresh clone path is documented and locally runnable: uv sync --locked, make check, representative query-explain/runtime-search.
make check and make audit-v02-gap-report pass after each shipped slice.
records/*.jsonl remains the canonical agent record surface; generated build artifacts remain rebuildable and untracked.
Every important retrieval/answer behavior has positive and nearby negative fixtures or CLI smokes.
Curation and audit reports produce classified, actionable gaps instead of vague needs-more-content warnings.
Public-safety review finds no tenant URLs, customer data, screenshots, credentials, SAP exports, or copied proprietary documentation.
Final ship reports state exact proof boundaries and residual risks without implying exhaustive SAP certification.
verification_strategy: Repository guard and schema validation for source records.
audit-completeness and v0.2 gap report for coverage/gap boundaries.
evaluate-fixtures, evaluate-runtime-retrieval, evaluate-answer-scenarios, evaluate-consultant-answers, and evaluate-semantic-models for behavior proof.
Focused tests for repo vision/design principles, clone-first docs, runtime ranking, curation reports, and consultant-answer boundaries.
Direct CLI smoke tests for target prompts and nearby adversarial prompts before shipping user-facing behavior.
git diff --check, Ruff, pytest, and public-safety review before commit/push.

first_proof.statement: The repo already proves the local-first SAP context runtime pattern: 746 items validate, generated indexes rebuild, runtime retrieval and semantic fixtures pass, answer scenarios and consultant answers are gated, and full local checks pass.
current_evidence: docs/vision.json defines the repo design contract and agent-first product direction
commit 5d3f04c expanded consultant-answer coverage with evidence binding and 297 passing tests
commit 4b04d1f added a layer-specific consultant-answer vision
make check and make audit-v02-gap-report passed after the consultant-answer slice
README documents clone/install, validation, runtime search, answer-scenario, and consultant-answer commands
first_proof.next_required_proof: Pick one bounded next slice that improves consumer trust or planner usability without broad content import: answer-profile schema, query-explain answer debug, source verification soft gate, or JSON consumer contract examples.

first_build_slices.summary: Move repeated consultant-answer support IDs, classifier triggers, required citations, and adversarial probes into a data-driven schema before adding many more answer domains.
Expose why a query or consultant-answer was ready/needs_curation, which evidence was kept/dropped, and which proof boundary decided the status.
Add machine-readable JSON examples showing how downstream agents consume bundles, query-explain, consultant-answer, citations, evidence, boundaries, and gaps.
Create an optional network-dependent source verification report that checks public pointers without making default make check flaky.
Use curation-report claim_maturity_index to move a bounded sample from L0/L1 toward L2/L3 with source/access/freshness/fail-closed improvements.
Promote exactly one next SAP domain only when existing evidence can support runtime fixtures, answer/bundle contracts, negative probes, and public-safe boundaries.

open_questions: Should the next slice prioritize data-driven answer profiles or downstream consumer JSON examples?
Which downstream consumer is the strongest forcing function: McCoy FO Generator v2, generic local agents, or a public clone-first demo?
Should source verification be release-only, a soft Make target, or a separate reviewer command?
Which domain has enough existing evidence to deserve the next deep slice without broad content import?
When should legacy YAML authoring be retired in favor of direct JSONL-native tools?

decision_log.decision: Keep docs/vision.json as the repo design contract and add this Go Vision as planning context rather than replacing the existing contract.
decision_log.reason: The existing contract is already covered by tests and documents product principles; Go Vision adds go-plan/go-task-friendly assumptions, proof boundaries, and first slices.

decision_log.decision: Prioritize verified behavior and consumer contracts over broad SAP content expansion.
decision_log.reason: The repository already has enough validated content to expose product gaps in answer, retrieval, curation, and consumer surfaces.

decision_log.decision: Retain JSON/JSONL-first artifacts for durable agent context.
decision_log.reason: Future agents and go-plan tasks need machine-readable constraints, not prose-only vision.

next_planning_boundary: Use go-plan for one bounded trust/consumer slice only. Recommended first: answer-profile-schema or consumer-contract-json-examples. Do not create broad SAP-content expansion tasks from this vision.
